Let me understand the bug more precisely to craft the right text. The crash is a use-of-uninitialized-value in `merge_out_clusters` called from `reorder_marks_arabic`. 

The key insight: In the second round (reorder inplace), `merge_out_clusters(start, j)` reads `out_info[i].cluster` for `i` in `[start, j)`. After `swap_buffers`, `out_info` points to the old buffer with `out_len` = old len entries. If the decomposition round produced MORE glyphs than the original input (out_len > old len), then `j` (an index into the new buffer) could exceed `out_len`, reading uninitialized memory.

Wait, actually let me reconsider. After swap_buffers, `out_len` = old `len` (the original input length before decomposition). The new `info` buffer has `len` = new out_len (after decomposition). If decomposition increased the count, then new len > out_len. In `reorder_marks_arabic`, `end` can be up to new len. So `j` can be up to new len, which can exceed `out_len`. Then `merge_out_clusters(start, j)` reads `out_info[i].cluster` for `i` up to `j-1`, which can exceed `out_len` → uninitialized memory.

So I need text that:

3. Contains a character that decomposes into multiple characters (increasing the buffer length).
